Mayor, Dhaka City Corporation -----Petitioner
Vs.
Dhaka Metropolitan Rickshaw Drivers Welfare Samity ----- Opposite Party
full_judgment:
3. The relevant facts for disposal of the Rule, inter alia, are that the present opposite party as the plaintiff filed the Title Suit No. 321 of 1999 in the 4th Court of Assistant Judge, Dhaka for a decree for permanent injunction restraining the present petitioners from creating obstruction for putting rickshaws for which they have been permitted to run on the streets of Dhaka. The plaintiff further stated that in order to improve the condition of the members of Dhaka Metropolitan Rickshaw Drivers the Welfare Samity started a "Rickshaw Project" and for that purpose distributed 5,000 rickshaws to the members. The plaintiff samity then applied to the office of the defendants to issue Rickshaw licence to them but having found no response the plaintiff samity held meeting, procession, press conference, sit on protest etc. Lastly on 7-12-1996 filed memorandum before defendants, at that time the defendant No. 1 made assurance to the members of the plaintiff samity that until licences are issued to the members of plaintiffs samity they would be allowed to run Rickshaw without licence and the Rickshaws that have been seized would be released and the cases filed by the Corporation would be withdrawn. The aforesaid declaration of defendant No. 1 was published in the Daily Newspaper on 8-12-1996 namely Daily Khabar, Daily Nowroz etc. and in accordance with the assurance made by the defendants 5,000 Rickshaw of Plaintiff Samity are running in the city streets. No legal problem would be arisen, if licences are issued to those Rickshaws. Inspite of assurance of defendant No.1 the employees of the defendants making hindrance to the Rickshaw Derivers i.e. the member of the Plaintiff Samity in plying the Rickshaw as a result of which thousands of Rickshaw drivers became unemployed caused their financial sufferings. On 7-11-1999 the plaintiff issued notice to the defendants for implementation of the assurance made by defendant No.1 but without any result, rather the defendants instead of implementing the assurance, making hindrance to the member of the samity in plying Rickshaws on and from 5-4-1999 and, as such, it is necessary to pass an order of permanent injunction restraining the defendant from doing such illegal act. Hence, the plaintiff Samity was compelled to file the suit. 

 9. After considering the submissions made by the learned Advocate for the petitioners and also consider the application under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure and the Annexure therein including the impugned order dated 30-1-2000, it appears to me that the opposite party being the Dhaka Metropolitan Rickshaw Derivers Welfare Samity filed the Title Suit No. 321 of 1999 for a decree for permanent injunction restraining the present petitioner Mayor, Dhaka City Corporation and others not to obstruct running rickshaws on the streets of Dhaka who were once granted licence. It further appears from the plaint of the suit (Annexure-"A") that as per claim of the opposite party that the petitioner No. 1 promised in the year of 1986 that 88 thousand Rickshaws would be granted licence in the year of 1986 but until the year of 1999 licences were granted for 79 thousand and out of remaining 9 thousand Rickshaws 5 thousand Rickshaws licence were not issued by the corporation, hence the present plaintiff-opposite party aggrieved and sought for a permanent injunction restraining the corporation from running those Rickshaws even- though, at present (20121) the existing situation is much higher than that of the numbers existing in the year of 1996 or in 1999 .
